name: Sembly AI
tagline: Transcribe a call and produce structured minutes, tasks, and searchable topics

tiers.name: Basic
tiers.limits: Unlimited meeting hours; 5 upload hours per paid user; 1-year history; 3 native automations.

tiers.name: Pro
tiers.limits: Up to 40 users/workspace; 10 upload hours, 5 AI documents, 5 AI insights, 5 native automations, and 5 webhooks per paid user; 2-year history.

tiers.name: MAX
tiers.limits: Minimum 3 users, maximum 500; 15 upload hours, 40 AI documents, 40 AI insights, 20 automations, and 20 webhooks per paid user; unlimited history.

tiers.name: Enterprise
tiers.limits: Custom invoicing, security reviews, support, and success package; no public numeric price.

pricing.billingTerms: monthly + annual (annual advertised 30% lower); free trials offered with no duration published
pricing.hiddenCosts: MAX requires at least 3 paid users. Upload hours, AI documents, AI insights, automations, and webhooks remain per-user quotas despite unlimited meeting hours. The former $15 'Professional' plan on file is not in the current live lineup.

verdictSummary: The core loop is buildable, but a dependable replacement becomes a real weekend or multi-day project. For Sembly AI, transcribe a call and produce structured minutes, tasks, and searchable topics. The hard boundary is meeting bots, team collaboration, automations, and broad integrations, plus capture reliability, integrations, and collaboration.
coreLoopDIY: Record or import a call, transcribe it locally, identify speakers with manual correction, and produce structured minutes, tasks, and searchable topics.
requirements: optional OpenAI or Anthropic API key
whatYouLose: meeting bots, team collaboration, automations, and broad integrations
ongoingBurden: audio permissions, model updates, calendar APIs, storage, speaker correction, and sync
whyPeopleStillPay: People still pay for Sembly AI because a meeting tool must capture every call without surprising anyone, then make the result searchable and shareable across a team. The recurring cost buys audio permissions, model updates, calendar APIs, storage, speaker correction, and sync, not just the visible interface.

priorArt.name: whisper.cpp
priorArt.desc: Widely used local Whisper inference implementation suitable for private transcription.

alternatives.name: Meeting Transcriber
alternatives.desc: Turns a captured meeting into a transcript, summary, decisions and tasks in ordinary Markdown.

facts.install: On macOS 14.2+, trust the third-party Homebrew repository and install its cask, then grant microphone, Screen Recording and Accessibility permissions
facts.engines: WhisperKit or NVIDIA Parakeet TDT v3 for ASR; FluidAudio/CoreML for VAD, diarization and speaker embeddings; summaries via Claude Code CLI or any OpenAI-compatible endpoint such as Ollama or LM Studio
facts.dataFormat: Local dual-track WAV recordings, metadata JSON, raw TXT transcripts and structured Markdown protocols under the configured output folder
facts.gapVsPaid: It is macOS-only and lacks Sembly's collaborative cloud workspace, task integrations and calendar bot.
facts.setupBlocker: macOS 14.2+ only, multiple privacy permissions, a third-party Homebrew tap, model downloads and a separate Claude/Ollama/OpenAI-compatible setup for summaries

alternatives.name: Muesli
alternatives.desc: Local transcripts plus configurable notes, decisions and action items; the searchable notebook stays on your Mac.

facts.install: Download the notarized macOS app, move it to Applications, grant audio/accessibility permissions and download an on-device model
facts.engines: Local ASR includes Parakeet, Nemotron, Cohere Transcribe, Whisper via WhisperKit, Qwen3 ASR, SenseVoice, Indic ASR and experimental Gemma; summaries use OpenAI, OpenRouter, ChatGPT OAuth or local Ollama
facts.dataFormat: Recordings, dictation history, transcripts, notes and model caches in local macOS app storage; optional iCloud sync sends text but not audio, and optional summary providers receive transcript text
facts.gapVsPaid: It has no shared web workspace or team task integrations, and summary quality depends on the local or BYOK model configured.
facts.setupBlocker: Apple Silicon and several macOS permissions are mandatory; first use needs a model download, and cloud-quality summaries need an API key, ChatGPT login or local Ollama

alternatives.name: OpenWhispr
alternatives.desc: Records or imports audio, labels speakers, generates notes and keeps the result searchable.

facts.install: Install the signed macOS DMG, Windows EXE or Linux package, grant audio/accessibility permissions and choose local, cloud or BYOK processing
facts.engines: Local Whisper via whisper.cpp; NVIDIA Parakeet and Nemotron via sherpa-onnx; local LLMs via llama.cpp; BYOK OpenAI, Groq, xAI, Mistral, Tinfoil, OpenRouter, Corti, Anthropic/Google and OpenWhispr Cloud
facts.dataFormat: Notes and history in local SQLite with recordings/model caches in app directories; optional sync uses OpenWhispr Cloud/Neon PostgreSQL, while cloud or BYOK audio goes to the selected provider
facts.gapVsPaid: Its task and topic extraction and shared-team workflow are less mature than Sembly's managed minutes, and quality depends on chosen models and hardware.
facts.setupBlocker: Meeting capture needs OS audio permissions and a model download or cloud/API choice; macOS also needs Accessibility and Screen Recording/System Audio permission

alternatives.name: Speakr
alternatives.desc: Self-hosted transcription, templates, topics, tasks, search and chat in one polished web app.

facts.install: Download the example Docker Compose and .env, add transcription/text-model credentials or endpoints, set the admin account and run docker compose up -d
facts.engines: ASR via self-hosted WhisperX, OpenAI transcription, Mistral Voxtral, AssemblyAI, VibeVoice or custom endpoints; LLMs via any OpenAI-compatible endpoint including OpenRouter, OpenAI, Gemini, LocalAI or Ollama
facts.dataFormat: SQLite in the mounted instance directory, audio in mounted uploads or S3-compatible storage, and optional auto-exports such as Markdown and SRT files
facts.gapVsPaid: It is a self-hosted archive rather than a turnkey meeting bot, so capture and structured minutes depend on the ASR and LLM configuration.
facts.setupBlocker: Docker is mandatory for the easy path, and the operator must supply API keys or deploy a separate GPU ASR container plus reverse proxy/TLS

notes: Editorial comparison targets the Professional plan and a personal meeting notebook DIY substitute. Recheck price before merge.
prompt:
Build a personal replacement for Sembly AI in an empty repository.
Use Python 3.12, FastAPI, SQLite, whisper.cpp, and a minimal HTMX interface; do not offer alternative stacks.
The core loop is: record or import a call, transcribe it locally, identify speakers with manual correction, and produce structured minutes, tasks, and searchable topics.
Make the first run work locally with one documented command.
Store all user data locally by default and make export straightforward.
Put secrets in .env, ship .env.example, and never commit credentials.
Add explicit start, pause, resume, and stop controls with a visible recording indicator.
Support importing WAV, MP3, M4A, and MP4 files through ffmpeg.
Run transcription locally and display timestamped editable segments.
Let the user rename speakers and propagate corrections through the transcript.
Generate decisions, action items, questions, and a concise summary from approved text.
Export Markdown, plain text, and WebVTT beside the original recording.
Include clear empty, loading, success, and recoverable error states.
Add input validation, safe filenames, and graceful handling of unavailable APIs.
Write focused tests for the core transformation and one end-to-end happy path.
Create a README with setup, architecture, permissions, data location, and backup steps.
Do not add accounts, billing, telemetry, analytics, or a hosted control plane.
Deliberately leave out silent background capture.
Deliberately leave out automatic bot attendance in video meetings.
Deliberately leave out team workspaces and enterprise retention controls.
Finish by running the tests and listing the exact commands used.
